name: New Jersey

sales.rateNote: Single statewide rate: New Jersey has no general county or city sales tax. Reduced rates apply in Urban Enterprise Zones (3.3125% at certified sellers) and on qualifying in-person retail sales in Salem County (half rate).

local.levies: No general local sales tax. Special-area levies exist on top of the state rate: Atlantic City Luxury Tax, Cape May County Tourism Sales Tax (Wildwood, Wildwood Crest, North Wildwood), and hotel-only charges (State Occupancy Fee, optional Municipal Occupancy Tax, Meadowlands hotel assessment).
local.capNote: In Atlantic City, when both taxes apply, the state rate is reduced so the combined Luxury Tax + Sales Tax cannot exceed 12.625% (Division of Taxation, S&U-4).

groceries.note: Most food sold as grocery items is exempt; candy, soft drinks and prepared food are taxable. Items bought with SNAP benefits are exempt even if otherwise taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing and footwear for human use are exempt with no price cap. Fur clothing, accessories, sport/recreational equipment and most protective equipment remain taxable.

otherRates.item: Urban Enterprise Zone (UEZ) purchases from certified sellers
otherRates.note: Half the state rate on most taxable sales of tangible personal property by UEZ-certified businesses; order placed in person in the zone. Motor vehicles and energy excluded from UEZ benefits.

Half the regular rate on qualifying in-person retail sales of goods in Salem County; excludes motor vehicles, alcohol, cigarettes, online/mail-order sales, services, prepared food, lodging and cannabis.
ZEV exemption repealed by P.L. 2024, c. 19: 3.3125% from Oct. 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025, full 6.625% from July 1, 2025.
Charged in addition to Sales Tax in most municipalities (lower rates in Wildwoods, Newark, Jersey City, Atlantic City).

sales.holidayNote: No 2026 sales tax holiday appears in the Division of Taxation's 2026 news list (checked 2026-10-05).

useTax.note: Use Tax equals the Sales Tax rate in effect at purchase; due on out-of-state, online or mail purchases taxed at less than 6.625%. Residents may report it on the NJ-1040 using a published income-based table.

facts.text: Rate history: 7% from July 15, 2006, 6.875% during 2017, and 6.625% since January 1, 2018.
Shoppers pay half the normal rate (3.3125%) on many purchases at UEZ-certified businesses; the program is run by the Department of Community Affairs' UEZ Authority.
Electric cars lost their exemption: zero emission vehicles were taxed at 3.3125% from October 1, 2024 and at the full 6.625% from July 1, 2025.
Since January 1, 2026, a $3 per day surcharge applies to taxable hotel stays in first-class cities with an international airport, currently only Newark.
Atlantic City levies a 9% Luxury Tax (3% on drinks sold by the glass); combined with the state tax it cannot exceed 12.625%.
Disposable paper products (towels, napkins, toilet tissue, paper plates) are exempt when bought for household use.

property.levied: Local: municipal tax assessors value property and municipalities levy and collect the tax for the municipality, county and school districts; the state Division of Taxation (Property Administration) and county boards of taxation oversee assessment. No state property tax levy.

assessment.text: Property is assessed at 'true value' (market value) as of October 1 of the pre-tax year. Because municipalities revalue at different times, the state publishes an annual equalization table; on appeal an assessment is tested against the district's average ratio within a common level range of plus or minus 15%.

homestead.name: ANCHOR (Affordable New Jersey Communities for Homeowners and Renters)
homestead.text: New Jersey has no general homestead exemption on the bill; relief is paid as a benefit. For the 2025 ANCHOR year, homeowners with income of $150,000 or less get $1,500 and those with $150,001–$250,000 get $1,000; renters get $450 ($700 if 65+) with income up to $150,000.
homestead.applyBy: 2025 application deadline: November 2, 2026 (Division of Taxation; many under-65 applicants are filed automatically).

otherRelief.name: Stay NJ (homeowners 65+)
otherRelief.text: For the 2025 tax year, maximum benefit $6,500 (income up to $100,000), $5,000 ($100,000.01–$150,000), $4,000 ($150,000.01–$200,000); paid in February and May 2027. Applied for on combined Form PAS-1.

otherRelief.name: Senior Freeze (Property Tax Reimbursement)
otherRelief.text: Reimburses eligible seniors and disabled persons for increases in property tax on their main home over their base year; part of the combined PAS-1 application.

otherRelief.name: $250 senior/disabled and $250 veteran deductions; 100% disabled veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: Municipally administered deductions from the property tax bill, plus a full exemption for 100% disabled veterans.

facts.text: The combined total of ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, Stay NJ and the senior/veteran deductions cannot exceed the property taxes paid on the main home for the year.
The FY2027 budget (signed June 30, 2026) split the remaining 2026 Stay NJ payment into halves paid in August and November 2026, lowering the total 2026 benefit.

Assessment appeals go to the County Board of Taxation by April 1 (May 1 after a revaluation; January 15 in Burlington, Gloucester and Monmouth); assessments over $1 million may go straight to the Tax Court.
Municipalities set property values on October 1 for the following tax year; improvements made later can trigger an 'added assessment'.
Stay NJ is limited to owners aged 65+ who lived in the home all 12 months of 2025 with income up to $200,000; renters are not eligible.

uncertain: S&U-4 (Sales Tax Guide) is dated Rev. 07/22; its grocery, clothing, Salem County, Atlantic City and occupancy-fee rules were not contradicted by newer pages but the bulletin itself has not been reissued.
Statewide property tax due dates (quarterly installments) not found on a Division of Taxation page read for this file; left null.
No official Division of Taxation page explicitly states 'no sales tax holiday in 2026'; the note relies on the absence of any announcement in the 2026 news list.
Exact amounts of the Senior Freeze reimbursement and income limits not recorded (income standards page not read).
